sentences.text: Background 2.

As gleaned from application read with Final Report under section 279/337/304A IPC, deceased Sanu Kumari riding Auto No.DL-1RN-4806 suffered fatal injuries in a motor vehicle accident in front of Police Line, Vikas Puri, Delhi on 28.12.2016 after the auto driver failed to control the vehicle which overturned after hitting the e-Rickshaw resulting in bodily injuries to passengers travelling in the Auto.

Complainant Danish was shifted to DDU Hospital, Hari Nagar, New Delhi where nature of injury upon MLC No.12760/16 was opined 'simple'
whereas Sanu Kumari admitted at Mata Channan Devi Hospital,
Delhi upon MLC No.7959/16 was declared 'Brought Dead'.
3. FIR No.695/2016 under section 279/337/304A IPC was registered at PS Vikas Puri on 29.12.2016 and site-plan was prepared by the IO.

entities.text: DDU Hospital, Hari Nagar, New Delhi
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: E-Rickshaw seized from the spot was released on superdari after its mechanical inspection and offence under section 179 M.V. Act was added against registered owner Rajpal Mathur who claimed to have sold the vehicle to Mahender S/o Nand Ram.

Notice under section 133 M.V. Act was served upon 2nd owner who claimed to have sold the vehicle to Rahul S/o Pappan AND proceedings under section 82 & 83 Cr.P.C was MACT No.872/2017 Foujdar Mahto & Anr. Vs. Rahul & Anr.

sentences.text: Page No. 2 of 15  initiated against Rahul S/o Ganesh (driver) who failed to join proceedings despite NBW issued by concerned Court.
Documents viz. RC, Permit & Fitness were verified from concerned authorities and dead body of Sanu Kumari was handed over to its relative after postmortem examination.
Separate Kalandra for offence under section 146/196 M.V Act was prepared against Rajpal Mathur after he failed to produce valid policy.

IO, thereafter, concluded investigation and prepared DAR which was filed in Court along with copy of Final Report under section 279/304A IPC read with 146/196 & 179 M.V. Act.
4.

It is submitted that deceased Sanu Kumari @ Sonam Kumari, aged 20 years, was earning Rs.9,724/- per month by doing private job and respondents driver & registered owner are jointly & severally liable to compensate petitioners for the untimely death of their daughter due to fatal injuries suffered in motor vehicle accident.
Defence 5.
Respondent Rahul S/o Ganesh being absconder did not join proceedings.

6. Respondent Rajpal Mathur (registered owner), on the other hand, has denied liability to compensate petitioners by contending sale of Bajaj Three Wheller TSR No.DL-1RN-4806 which was insured with Reliance General Insurance Co. Ltd. till 28.08.2016 to Mahender S/o Nand Ram for sale consideration Rs.1,10,000/-.

20. FINDING: Issue No.1 is therefore decided by holding that death of Sanu Kumari @ Sonam Kumari was caused due to fatal injuries suffered in motor vehicle accident on 28.12.2016 as a result of rash and negligent driving of TSR No.DL-1RN-4806 by respondent Rahul (driver) which vehicle was registered in the name of Rajpal Mathur (owner) and not insured against 'Third Party Risks'.

opennyai_summary.facts:
As gleaned from application read with Final Report under section 279/337/304A IPC, deceased Sanu Kumari riding Auto No.DL-1RN-4806 suffered fatal injuries in a motor vehicle accident in front of Police Line, Vikas Puri, Delhi on 28.12.2016 after the auto driver failed to control the vehicle which overturned after hitting the e-Rickshaw resulting in bodily injuries to passengers travelling in the Auto.
Complainant Danish was shifted to DDU Hospital, Hari Nagar, New Delhi where nature of injury upon MLC No.12760/16 was opined 'simple'
whereas Sanu Kumari admitted at Mata Channan Devi Hospital,
Delhi upon MLC No.7959/16 was declared 'Brought Dead'.
3. FIR No.695/2016 under section 279/337/304A IPC was registered at PS Vikas Puri on 29.12.2016 and site-plan was prepared by the IO.
E-Rickshaw seized from the spot was released on superdari after its mechanical inspection and offence under section 179 M.V. Act was added against registered owner Rajpal Mathur who claimed to have sold the vehicle to Mahender S/o Nand Ram.
Notice under section 133 M.V. Act was served upon 2nd owner who claimed to have sold the vehicle to Rahul S/o Pappan AND proceedings under section 82 & 83 Cr.P.C was MACT No.872/2017 Foujdar Mahto & Anr. Vs. Rahul & Anr.
Separate Kalandra for offence under section 146/196 M.V Act was prepared against Rajpal Mathur after he failed to produce valid policy.
It is submitted that deceased Sanu Kumari @ Sonam Kumari, aged 20 years, was earning Rs.9,724/- per month by doing private job and respondents driver & registered owner are jointly & severally liable to compensate petitioners for the untimely death of their daughter due to fatal injuries suffered in motor vehicle accident.
Respondent Rahul S/o Ganesh being absconder did not join proceedings.

opennyai_summary.issue:
i. Whether Sanu Kumari @ Sonam Kumari  sustained fatal injuries in a motor vehicle  accident dt. 28.12.2016 due to rash and  negligent driving of vehicle no.DL-1RN-  4806 being driven by respondent no.1  Rahul and owned by respondent no.2  Rajpal Mathur?
...OPP  ii.
Whether
the petitioner in the above  mentioned case is entitled to claim  compensation, if so, what amount and from  whom? ...
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Foujdar Mahto & Anr. Vs. Rahul & Anr.
Adverse inference is therefore required to be raised against the driver as per the dicta of Hon'ble High Court of Orissa in National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Durdadshya Kumar Samal & Ors.
1987
Ori . 57 AND Cholamandalam MS General Insurance Co. Vs. Smt. Kamlesh & Ors. decided by Hon'ble High Court of Delhi on 11th November, 2008.
17. It is all the more well settled law that negligence of the driver in case of road traffic accident is required to be established on the touchstone of preponderance of probability and standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt does not apply to claim petitions under Motor Vehicle Act as held by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in para 15 of Bimla Devi & Ors. Vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Ors (2009) 13 SCC 530.
MACT No.872/2017 Foujdar Mahto & Anr. Vs. Rahul & Anr.
She had, therefore, completed 21 years of age at the time of death and Multiplier of 18 will apply in the case as held in para 19 read with para 42 of Sarla Verma & Ors vs. DTC (2009) 6 SCC 121 which has been approved by the Constitution Bench of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in para 42 of National Insurance Co.
Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi (2017) 16 SCC 680.
Vs. DTC (2009) 6 SCC 121 which have been affirmed by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in para 41 of National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi (Supra).
In view of the law/guidelines laid down in (i) Pranay Sethi (Supra) read with (ii) Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd vs. Nanu Ram (2018) 18 SCC 130 AND (iii) United India Insurance Co. Ltd. vs Satinder Kaur (2021) 11 SCC 780, a sum of Rs.48,400 x 02 = Rs.96,800/- (Rupees Ninety Six Thousand & Eight Hundred only) is awarded to petitioners as compensation under the head 'loss of consortium'.
There is nothing on record to justify withholding interest on the award amount.
opennyai_summary.arguments: 16. Respondents Rahul (driver) and Rajpal Mathur (owner), on the other hand, have neither availed their right to cross-examine witnesses nor led any evidence to rebut allegation of rash and negligent driving of TSR No.DL-1RN-4806 resulting in fatal injuries suffered by Sanu Kumari @ Sonam Kumari who was declared 'Brought Dead' upon MLC No.7959/16 prepared at Mata Channan Devi Hospital, Janak Puri, New Delhi.
